sources.note: A commentary in this corpus states the pairing in its own text, usually as 'English (Original)'. These renderings carry a locator and are re-checked by scripts/synthesis_lexicon.py --check, which is why they are the only kind the machine can verify. They are also the only kind that proves a rendering is actually in use here rather than merely available.

Terms this repository already asserted before the lexicon existed. Migrated rather than re-derived, so the seed carries no outside knowledge: every one of these was already in a file under version control. Unverifiable in the sense that no locator points at a commentary using it - but not unsourced.

Heidegger's epoch of being. Distinct from Husserl's Epoché, which it transliterates onto; the -de suffix disambiguates the slug, and the accent is the only thing that separates the two words in print.

The theme registry records that English renderings diverge sharply between translations, so a search keyed to one of them drops whole commentaries. This entry is where that divergence belongs; add a translator field as each attribution is established from a commentary rather than assumed.
Three commentaries, three renderings of one term, all attested. A theme registered with any one of them finds a third of the passages. This entry is the argument for the lexicon in miniature.
